subject: Live admin telemetry evidence request — export formats, retention, and redaction options
messages:
From: Elaine Porter <elaine.porter@acmehealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@acmehealth.com
Date: 2025-05-11T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: live admin telemetry and operator-change evidence for upcoming audit

Hi Lauren / team,

We're preparing for our Q3 SOC 2 readiness review and need a slightly deeper view into Redwood's admin telemetry. Specifically Acme's auditors have asked for: a) a near-real-time export of operator-change events (modify/add/remove privilege, assume-role, console session start/stop), b) a 90-day retention snapshot with checksums, and c) a sample of redacted payloads that demonstrate PII/username handling.

Could you confirm what fields are logged for console operator events, available export formats (streaming vs batch), and options for pre-redaction vs post-export redaction? Ideally we'd like to see a small sample (one day's worth) next week so the controls team can validate redaction before the full delivery.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Porter
Sr. Compliance Manager — Acme Health

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Porter <elaine.porter@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-11T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: live admin telemetry and operator-change evidence for upcoming audit

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear ask. High level answers and proposed next steps below.

What we log for console/operator activity (examples):
- event_id, timestamp (ISO), operator_user_id (internal id), operator_identity_type (human/service), action (role_assume / privilege_change / session_start / session_end / api_key_rotate), resource_target (user_id/team_id/instance), ip_address, region, request_summary, request_payload_hash, result_status (success/fail), request_latency_ms

Export modes we support:
1) Streaming (Kafka-like push to a customer-managed endpoint / secure TLS) — near-real-time, low-latency. Good for live monitoring.
2) Periodic snapshot (daily JSONL or Parquet bundles, gzipped, with a signed manifest + SHA256 checksums). Good for audited deliveries.

Redaction options:
- Pre-export pseudonymization: we can hash user identifiers with per-customer salt (KMS-backed) so data leaves already pseudonymized.
- Field-level masking: redact fields marked PII (email, full name) inline (irreversible) before export.
- Post-export redaction: export raw, then deliver a redacted derivative — not preferred for PoC but possible under an encrypted handoff and attested manifest.

Suggested plan for Acme:
- Week of May 19: deliver a one-day sample (gzipped JSONL, 1–2MB) with pre-export pseudonymization and a signed manifest.
- May 26: provide 90-day aggregated snapshot export options (daily Parquet bundles, partitioned by date + tenant) and a document describing retention/rotation policy.

Attachments: attaching a tiny sample schema (requested_schema_v1.jsonl) and a manifest template for your auditors to review.

Open questions for your auditors:
- Are per-record plaintext usernames required in the sample, or will pseudonymized ids suffice for review?
- Do they require streaming ingestion (SSE/Kafka) or just secure SFTP delivery of daily bundles?

If that's agreeable I'll loop in Karthik + Ben to scope throughput, estimated bundle sizes, and the redaction implementation.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
Attachments: requested_schema_v1.jsonl (schema stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Elaine Porter <elaine.porter@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2025-05-11T12:28:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: RE: Request: live admin telemetry and operator-change evidence for upcoming audit

Lauren — forwarding with some infra specifics and questions inline.

On pre-export pseudonymization: we use per-customer KMS-derived salts to HMAC operator_user_id. That preserves stable mapping for duration of retention window but is irreversible without the salt. For Acme we can:
- Option A (recommended): HMAC(user_id) + preserve plaintext operator_role (so auditors can verify role changes without real usernames).
- Option B: full name/email redaction (mask to <redacted>) where auditors want zero PII in the ledger.

Export format tradeoffs:
- JSONL (newline-delimited) is easiest for samples and small customers — human readable and quick to validate.
- Parquet is significantly smaller for large windows and supports schema evolution; recommended for 90-day snapshots.

Operational constraints / costs:
- Expected daily volume: ~20–80k operator events for a mid-sized tenant during business hours. A gzipped Parquet day ~50–120MB depending on field inclusion. We'll provide estimates after a 48h instrumentation run.

Delivery / verification:
- We will produce a signed manifest (SHA256 per file + signed manifest file encrypted with your public key), and an overall manifest signature from Redwood's signing key.
- We support SFTP, presigned S3 URLs (time-limited), or push to a customer-managed Kafka over TLS.

Attachments: export_manifest_template.csv (contains fields, example checksums, and expected file names).

Action items:
- Lauren: confirm which redaction option Acme prefers for the sample (A or B).
- Ben / Monica: please run a 48h capture on the prod console telemetry (pseudonymize at capture point if option A) and report size/partitioning recommendations by EOD Friday.

Karthik
Head of Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
Attachments: export_manifest_template.csv
